summary: Aermotor LS-40 tower built in 1936 near Timmonsville, sold by the SC Forestry Commission in the late 1990s, and now re-erected on private land in Sumter County.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with a 7x7 foot steel cab; reconstructed to 40 feet on its original concrete footings (formerly 100 feet)
facts.agency: South Carolina Forestry Commission (original owner; sold in the late 1990s)

access.note: Owned by Billy McIntosh and re-erected on his property; the register says it is used as a hunting and wildlife observation spot, and no public access is described

events.note: Register gives 1936; Forest Lookouts newspaper items show equipment moved to the site in March 1936 and a CCC camp working on the site in April 1936
Registered February 24, 2013 as US 970, SC 23; nominated by Michael T. Finch, Jr., FFLA Area Rep

corrections.proposed: South Carolina Forestry Commission (original owner); now privately owned by Billy McIntosh
corrections.why: A person who owns the tower is not an agency. The register names McIntosh as owner and administrator and says the Forestry Commission sold him the tower in the late 1990s.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts' 1936 newspaper items describe a 100-foot tower; the register says it was later reconstructed to 40 feet on its original footings. Both describe the same tower at different times.
The register places the original site near Timmonsville in Florence County and the current site in Sumter County. The tower moved, so both are correct.

The Commission's own history dates the closure of its fire tower system to October 1, 1993; a Post and Courier piece says the system was decommissioned in 1994. The story uses the Commission's date and reports the newspaper's.

notes_for_editor: The sale is undated in the sources: 'late 1990s' per the register and '199??' per Forest Lookouts. It is left out of events until a year can be sourced. The record's agency field holds the owner's name, so a correction is proposed for a human to apply. The 40-foot height is the current structure; the register does not give the year of the reconstruction. No staffing names or fires beyond the 1936 towerman notice were found. Used 1 WebSearch and about 4 page reads.
